text: Quarantined obsolete Blue Ridge MU plugin: unguarded request data entered shell_exec. Removed unnecessary unrestricted rsync sudo and expired unlisted privileged jpark account. No corroborated malicious login in baseline.
Database grants separate WordPress and billing; dump archive encrypted but temporary plaintext tar created in a traversable directory. Reviewing job permissions and invoice provenance.

Only the hidden branch of rental-quote.php returns the DB settings. Removed that branch while preserving normal pricing; app DB credential rotated and report.cnf synchronized. Root orders job no longer executes application PHP.

Release uses tar over SSH without an agent; maintenance sources local root-owned steps, not the site. No evidence of a foreign CI login. Scoping git privileges and the exposed credential in repository config.

Eight pre-existing invoice/order discrepancies, no recent adjusting user in logs; do not mass-rewrite shop data. Constrained invoice corrections to the authoritative order amount and made database dump/tar output root-only.
Restricted dump key to write-only rsync from db-01. Removed world access to repository/token and changed git maintenance to run without root. Verify next scheduled dump/release.
MariaDB now records connections and table access without logging row contents or SQL passwords. Confirmed 17:30 encrypted archive transfer, settlement, and manifest checks succeeded.

Committed the two reviewed customer endpoints (e99f2e7) to main. Release now uses an exact commit and unprivileged, deletion-aware rsync rather than overlaying a tarball that left unmanaged PHP in service; no SSH agent forwarding.

Jpark is absent from the current staff directory. Kept account data but expired Unix access on web and CI, removed WP admin, invalidated passwords/sessions and disabled WP login/reset for the inactive account.
Restricted the WordPress SQL identity from the entire 10.20.0 subnet to the web-01 address used by the application and its reporting jobs. No billing grant to that identity.

Node exporter now serves localhost and office addresses, not the public address; dashboard remains available. Incoming release key is source-bound with forwarding disabled, no change to staff password access.

CI release identity had its outbound key authorized for inbound access to CI itself despite zero such logins; removed that self-login path without changing release authentication. Sticky shared repository prevents developers unlinking root-owned config or hooks.

Preserved original PHP files, hashes, and relevant access lines under /root/ir. The 174.205 source returned for a POST after quarantine and got a full homepage, not the 159-byte support reply. No SSH login from either quote source or the support source.
Pinned CI SSH host key after matching the archive client fingerprint against ci-01 directly. Confirmed prior dump hashes match on both hosts and decrypt to both expected SQL members.
Verified CI release client host key against web-01 locally, switched from accept-new to strict existing host key checking. 17:39 scheduled release completed OK.

No available trusted public TLS certificate was found on-host; do not force a self-signed replacement that strands staff and customers. Owner to confirm TLS termination at provider or provision trusted TLS for WordPress and Grafana.

17:40 check: ten payouts accepted on db-01, web reconciliation healthy, encrypted archive on CI. No evidence of billing key, bucket key, CI token, deploy password, or root-only secrets read; did not rotate unrelated staff credentials.
17:43 follow-up: no new unknown SQL client, same digest for 17:40 archive on sender and receiver, and normal bookkeeper and ops activity. No sign of unauthorized billing or DB login.

External bucket endpoint has had no route since before migration; the 17:41 job confirmed this persists, independent of the DB-to-CI transfer. Do not treat successful local archive arrival as verified external redundancy.

Shift close: reviewed code hash still matches CI. Last observed repeat of the quote request got a normal 127-byte result; 17:44 reconciliation and customer ride page healthy. Keep quarantined files out of replacement images.
